::: {.bio}
*I am an Assistant Professor at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical
Medicine.*
*I did my PhD in the optimal usage of the BCG vaccine, transitioning to work on
real-time modelling of infectious disease outbreaks on the 3rd of January
2020.*
*Four days later, I switched to work on what was then known as 2019-NCoV.*
*I did early work on the size and scale of the initial outbreak, tracking
transmissions in different countries, and exploring the potential role of
different interventions.*
*Throughout the pandemic, I ran a dashboard that was used by over a million
people.*
*I also provided estimates, forecasts, and analyses weekly to the UK government
advisory bodies.*
*I developed the tools and methods we used into open source software and these
were used by upwards of 30 public health agencies around the world.*
*I have continued to work in this area with a focus on improving tools and
methods used both in research and in public health practice.*
*I have recently transitioned to Julia for my work and am exploring how to
propagate Julia based tools to the users of our current tooling and to the
wider infectious disease modelling community.*
:::

:::
:::

## The talks {.section-tight}

All three are on **Friday 14 August 2026** in **Muschel — N3**, times
Europe/Berlin.

::: {.grid .talk-row}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.talk-card}
[14:30–14:45]{.talk-time}

#### [A composable Julia ecosystem for infectious disease modelling](roadmap/index.qmd)

[A roadmap, challenges, and questions]{.talk-sub}

Where EpiAware is going, what we have got wrong so far, and the questions we
would like the Julia community to answer.

::: {.talk-card}
[14:45–15:00]{.talk-time}

#### [Estimating epidemiological delay distributions](delays/index.qmd)

[From R/Stan to Julia]{.talk-sub}

CensoredDistributions.jl, and an honest comparison with the R and Stan
implementation it grew out of.

[Page](delays/index.qmd){.btn .btn-sm .btn-outline-primary}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.talk-card}
[16:45–17:00]{.talk-time}

#### [Composable probabilistic models](composable/index.qmd)

[Lowering barriers to rigorous infectious disease modelling]{.talk-sub}

Why composition is how modelling evidence gets to be timely, rigorous and
collaborative at once.

## Other recent work you might like {.section-tight}

::: {.grid .links-row}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
##### Julia

- [CensoredDistributions.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/CensoredDistributions.jl)
  — censoring and truncation for Distributions.jl
- [ConvolvedDistributions.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/ConvolvedDistributions.jl)
  — the next layer up, combining delays
- [EpiAware](https://github.com/EpiAware) — the organisation these talks are
  about
- [EpiAwarePackageTools.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/EpiAwarePackageTools.jl)
  — one rigid package template
- [EpiAwareADTools.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/EpiAwareADTools.jl) —
  automatic differentiation as something you test
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
##### R

- [epinowcast](https://www.epinowcast.org/) — the ecosystem this is trying to
  become in Julia, with a
  [community forum](https://community.epinowcast.org/) and seminar series
- [primarycensored](https://primarycensored.epinowcast.org/) — the R and Stan
  package behind the delays talk
- [epidist](https://epidist.epinowcast.org/) — individual-level delay
  estimation
- [EpiNow2](https://epiforecasts.io/EpiNow2/) and
  [scoringutils](https://epiforecasts.io/scoringutils/) — widely used, and
  what I want a better foundation for
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
##### Papers and talks

- [A workflow for infectious disease modelling](https://github.com/seabbs/a-workflow-for-infectious-disease-modelling)
  — the paper behind the composable models talk
- [BVDOutbreakSize](https://github.com/epiforecasts/BVDOutbreakSize) —
  outbreak size for the 2026 Ebola outbreak in the DRC, in real time
- [How I am LLM](https://samabbott.co.uk/how-I-llm) — what coding agents do
  and do not do in a research workflow
- [How to serial interval?](https://samabbott.co.uk/how-to-serial-interval) —
  delays, censoring, and the serial interval as a composition
:::
:::
